pages.title: INTRODUCTION
pages.html:
INTRODUCTION

The Conversation Nobody Scores

Every line moves three things. Most people track zero.

You are in more high-stakes conversations than almost any professional alive.

Every showing is a conversation. Every offer is a conversation. Every negotiation, listing appointment, pipeline call, loan approval, family dinner after a showing — conversations. And every one of them is moving three scores simultaneously whether you are tracking them or not.

Profit. Love. Tax.

Those three scores determine the outcome of every transaction you have ever been in. Not the market. Not the rate environment. Not the inventory. The scores running underneath the conversation while the conversation is happening.

Most professionals lose deals they should have won. Not because they said the wrong thing. Because they were hearing words when they should have been watching the score. They were reacting to the surface when the real movement was happening underneath it.

◆

This book teaches you to watch the score.

It gives you the framework — Profit, Love, and Tax — built from the ground up so you understand not just what they are but why they move the way they move. It gives you the three signals that drive every score movement: Intent, Body, and Pressure. It gives you the six characters in every real estate transaction and how to read each one. And then it gives you the nine moves — the executable doctrine that a scorer runs in real time when the score is going the wrong direction.

Nine moves. That's what separates a professional who understands deals from a professional who controls them.

◆

This book does not require any prior reading. It starts from zero and ends with a complete instrument you carry into every room. A showing, a listing appointment, a negotiation, a pre-approval call, a kitchen table conversation with a family that has not yet decided — after this book you are never in those conversations the same way again.

The scorer does not hope conversations go well. The scorer runs the moves that make them go well.

That is the difference between theory and doctrine.

pages.title: PART ONE
pages.html:
PART ONE

The PLT Score Triangle

The single diagram that explains everything

The Three Scores

Every conversation you have ever had was running three scores at the same time.

Not one. Three. Simultaneously. And every line — every word spoken, every pause, every question asked or not asked — moved all three. The movement was happening whether you saw it or not. This book teaches you to see it.

◆

P R O F I T

Leverage · Frame · Position

Who controls the frame. Who has the information advantage. Who is closer to getting what they actually want.

L O V E

Trust · Credibility · Loyalty

The relationship account. Takes months to build and seconds to burn. The reason clients take your call on Sunday and accept your advice on Thursday.

T A X

Risk · Exposure · Obligation

What the conversation costs. Not in dollars — in risk, obligation, and exposure. The debt created by what was said, coming due whether or not it was intended.

AT THE CENTER OF THE TRIANGLE: THE CONVERSATION

Every conversation sits at the center of the triangle. Every line spoken moves all three points simultaneously. No score changes in isolation. When Profit moves, Love and Tax are affected. When Love burns, Profit and Tax follow. The three scores are not separate meters. They are one system.

The scorer watches all three at once. That is the complete skill.

The Three Signals

Intent. Body. Pressure.

Three scores run underneath every conversation. Three signals drive those scores. You do not need to know what someone is thinking to score their move. You need to read three things.

◆

INTENT — what they actually want from this line.

Not what the words say. What the words are for. The buyer who says "we're just looking" is not just looking. Their Intent is to reduce the pressure of the showing so they can evaluate without committing. The seller who says "we're not in a hurry" is not telling you about their timeline. Their Intent is to protect Profit by signaling that your urgency cannot be used against them. Read the position the person is trying to establish — not the words they used to establish it.

BODY — what their physical presence is telling you.

The buyer who slows down in the kitchen is giving you information their mouth has not provided yet. The seller who crosses their arms when the price is mentioned is telling you the number triggered something. The loan officer who pauses before answering a question about timeline is calculating something they have not said. Body is not about microexpressions — it is about pace and energy. Does the room feel faster or slower after that line? Is the energy building or draining? The room's energy moves before the words confirm it.

PRESSURE — what external force is acting on this conversation.

The buyer who saw another offer come in this morning is under different Pressure than the buyer who is the only offer. The seller who has already bought their next house is under different Pressure than the seller with nowhere to go. The agent whose quarter is ending is under different Pressure than the agent who closed three deals last week. The person who appears to be negotiating from logic is almost always negotiating from Pressure. Find the Pressure and you find the real position.

◆

Intent. Body. Pressure. Read all three on every line. Then score the move. The scorer is not slower than the conversation. The scorer is inside the conversation at a level the other person is not operating on.

pages.title: PART TWO
pages.html:
PART TWO

The Six Characters

Every person in the transaction. How to read them.

01

The Buyer

The Buyer is the most emotionally exposed person in the transaction. They are spending the largest sum of money they have ever committed to in the shortest decision window they have ever been given. They are running fear, hope, excitement, and doubt simultaneously. Every line they say is driven by all four.

The Buyer's Profit position is almost always weaker than they believe. Their research gave them vocabulary. Vocabulary and leverage are not the same thing.

What the Buyer actually wants: certainty that they are not making a mistake. Everything else is a vehicle for that one thing. The buyer who keeps asking the same question in different forms is not confused about the answer. They are looking for certainty that the answer is right. The agent who understands this stops answering the question and starts building the certainty. Those are not the same move.

◆

Reading the Buyer's score in real time:

Profit — are they asking questions or making statements? Questions mean evaluation. Statements mean decision. The shift from questions to statements is the Profit signal that commitment is forming.

Love — are they telling you things they have no strategic reason to tell you? Personal details about why they want the house, how they imagine the space. Oversharing is Love. They trust you enough to give you information that does not help their negotiating position.

Tax — are they asking about problems before there are problems? These are Tax questions. The buyer is calculating exposure. Answer them honestly before they become urgent.

02

The Seller

The Seller is protecting something. Not just the price — the price is the number their protection is expressed through. What they are protecting is the meaning the property carries. The years of equity. The improvements. The specific memory of the house as the thing they built when everything else was uncertain. They are not selling a house. They are quantifying their own story.

The Seller's default position is distrust. Not distrust of the agent specifically — distrust of the transaction. They have heard stories. They know someone who felt they left money on the table. They arrive at this conversation with accumulated skepticism about the category of person sitting across from them.

The agent who leads with credentials feeds that skepticism. The agent who leads with honesty about the market, about the specific challenges of this property, about what the seller should expect — that agent builds Love faster than any other move available.

◆

Reading the Seller's score:

Profit — are they citing comps or citing memory? Comps are a Profit move. Memory is a validation seek. Read the difference.

Love — the first time a seller says "what do you think I should do" instead of telling you their plan, Love has moved. Small signal. Real movement.

Tax — every condition a seller adds is Tax being shifted to the buyer. Find out if they are protecting against a known risk or testing how much Tax the buyer will absorb.

03

The Agent

The Agent is the only person in the transaction who is in every conversation. Buyer, seller, loan officer, BDM, and indirectly in the family conversation when the client describes what their agent said at dinner. The agent's score runs across all of these simultaneously. A Love account burned with a seller at 2pm shows up in the buyer conversation at 5pm because the agent carries it with them.

The Agent's most common scoring error: confusing activity with position. The agent who calls every day is running high activity. If those calls provide genuine information — real updates, honest assessments — the activity builds Love. If those calls are the agent managing their own anxiety about the deal, the client starts to feel that. Activity without information is Tax. You are spending the client's attention without giving them value in return.

◆

The Agent's score runs on three things: Expertise builds Profit. Honesty builds Love. Patience manages Tax. The agent who maintains all three simultaneously is running the highest-value position in the transaction.

04

The Loan Officer

The Loan Officer runs the highest-stakes single conversation in the transaction. Not because it carries the most emotion — the offer does. But because the Loan Officer's conversation determines whether everything else proceeds or stops. The approval, the rate, the timeline, the conditions — all of it lives in conversations they control.

The Loan Officer's most dangerous move: false certainty. "You're going to be fine." These are not reassurances. They are Tax being transferred that they cannot always carry. The buyer told they were going to be fine who then hits an underwriting condition does not hear "this is normal process." They hear: you lied to me.

The Loan Officer who says "here are the three things that could affect your timeline and here is exactly what we do if any of them happen" carries higher Tax in the moment and infinitely more Love over the life of the transaction. Named Tax is manageable. Unnamed Tax compounds until it becomes a crisis.

05

The BDM

The BDM's job is to make conversations possible that would not otherwise happen. They are relationship infrastructure. Their conversations are almost never about properties. They are about trust, positioning, and the slow accumulation of Profit and Love that eventually becomes a referral, a repeat client, a partnership that generates pipeline.

The BDM scores every conversation as a long-term investment. A conversation with a builder representative that produces nothing today may produce five listings in eighteen months. The BDM who measures their score only by what happened immediately is tracking the wrong metric.

The BDM's primary tool: information given freely before it is asked for. The person who told you something important before it cost you anything not to know it — nobody forgets that person. That is the BDM's signature Love move.

06

The Family

The Family is the most underestimated participant in the transaction. They are not at the showing. Their name is not on the offer. But they are in every conversation the buyer or seller has before they go to sleep, and the score running in those conversations determines what the client believes when they wake up.

The spouse who has not seen the house is running pure Tax. They did not fall in love with the kitchen. They are calculating exposure — financial, logistical, emotional — with no Love to offset it. They are the most skeptical person in the transaction and they have the most influence over the person you are working with.

Watch the client's behavior after they talk to family. If the client's questions shift — if they start asking things they were not asking before — the family has introduced new Tax into the conversation. Find it. Name it. Manage it before it becomes the reason the deal dies.

The question a buyer asks after talking to their mother is almost always the mother's question, not the buyer's. Score it accordingly.

pages.title: PART THREE
pages.html:
PART THREE

The 9 Dominant Moves

The executable doctrine. Runs in real time. Under pressure. In the room.

Theory lives in books. Moves live in rooms.

The scorer does not leave the conversation to calculate. The scorer runs a move. These are the nine moves a scorer runs when the score turns — when Profit is slipping, Love is burning, or Tax is spiking. Each one is named. Each one is executable. Each one is yours to carry into every room you enter.

MOVE 01 · THE FRAME RESET

WHEN TO RUN IT Profit is collapsing because someone else defined the conversation.

Shift the category the conversation is happening inside. Do not fight the position that was taken. Move the ground it was taken on.

THE SITUATION Client after receiving an offer:

"That offer is insulting."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS You did not argue the emotion. You changed the frame the emotion lives inside. The client's position was built on feelings. Your new frame is built on data. Data versus emotion — data wins if you hold the frame.

The question is not how the offer feels. The question is what the market says.

MOVE 02 · THE HONEST STRIKE

WHEN TO RUN IT Love is fragile or starting to burn.

Tell the difficult truth before it becomes a surprise. Not after the inspection. Not after the appraisal. Before the client has any reason to distrust you.

THE SITUATION Before a showing, agent to buyer:

"There's something about this house I want you to understand before you get attached to it."

PROFIT —|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS People trust the person who tells them what others would hide. The Honest Strike is the fastest Love-building move in professional conversations. It costs nothing in Profit because it does not change your position — it elevates your credibility. The client who receives an Honest Strike becomes the client who defends you to their family.

Tell them the hard thing before they find it themselves.

MOVE 03 · THE INTELLIGENCE TRANSFER

WHEN TO RUN IT The client needs leverage they do not have.

Give the client information that improves their position before they ask for it. Not information that helps you close — information that helps them decide correctly.

THE SITUATION Agent to buyer at the start of a showing:

"The sellers already bought their next house. That matters for how we structure the offer."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX —

WHY IT WORKS This is one of the highest-value professional moves available because it simultaneously builds Profit and Love. Profit because the client now has a negotiating anchor. Love because you gave them something before they knew to ask for it. The agent who does not run Intelligence Transfer is working harder to close less.

Give them the information that gives them the edge.

MOVE 04 · THE EVIDENCE MIRROR

WHEN TO RUN IT Someone is anchored emotionally or irrationally.

Let them reach the conclusion themselves. Do not argue the position. Hand them the evidence and ask them what they see.

THE SITUATION Seller anchored above market at listing appointment:

"Let's look at the last six homes that sold on this block together."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS The Evidence Mirror works because people believe conclusions they reach themselves more than conclusions presented to them. You are not telling them they are wrong. You are letting the market tell them. The Profit gain comes from controlling the information. The Love gain comes from the fact that you did not make them feel corrected.

Hand them the evidence. Ask them what they see.

MOVE 05 · THE OWNERSHIP MOVE

WHEN TO RUN IT You made a mistake or your credibility slipped.

Own the error immediately and completely. No qualifications. No deflection. No context that softens it into not-quite-your-fault.

THE SITUATION Agent after a missed deadline:

"I should have caught that earlier. That's on me."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▲▲

WHY IT WORKS This is the fastest Love recovery in existence. Most professionals will not run it because it feels like weakness. It is the opposite. The person who owns an error before being asked to own it holds the frame — the other side came ready to argue and there is nothing to argue against. Tax increases because you have accepted responsibility. But the Love gain is so dominant that this is always the correct move. A small Tax increase for a major Love recovery is the best trade in the Scorer system.

Own it completely. Once. Without explanation.

MOVE 06 · THE PRESSURE REVEAL

WHEN TO RUN IT Someone's behavior does not match their words.

Surface the pressure shaping the conversation. Name it gently and directly. Not as an accusation — as a read.

THE SITUATION Buyer asking questions about inspection but hesitating on timeline:

"It sounds like the timeline might be the real concern here."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS The Pressure Reveal works because most people are not fully conscious of the pressure they are operating under. When you name it, two things happen: they feel understood, and the real conversation can begin. Profit builds because you have demonstrated that you read below the surface. Love builds because being seen is one of the most powerful human experiences. Tax drops because the hidden concern is now visible and therefore manageable.

Name the real conversation. Not the spoken one.

MOVE 07 · THE FAMILY INCLUSION

WHEN TO RUN IT A hidden decision-maker has appeared.

Bring the invisible participant into the process before they become the reason the deal does not close.

THE SITUATION Buyer mid-showing revealing his wife has not seen the house:

"Can we get her here this week? I want her to feel it too."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS Most deals do not die in the negotiation. They die in a kitchen conversation the agent never sees. The Family Inclusion move eliminates that conversation by creating a better one — one the agent is part of. Profit builds because you have controlled the timeline variable. Love builds because the framing ("I want her to feel it too") signals that you are working for the family, not against it. Tax drops because the unknown becomes scheduled.

Bring the invisible decision-maker into the room.

MOVE 08 · THE PATIENCE PLAY

WHEN TO RUN IT The other side is revealing their position.

Do nothing. Let them speak. The first person to reveal their full position loses leverage. The Patience Play is the only move that requires no action — only discipline.

THE SITUATION After submitting an offer, the listing agent calls:

"... [silence] ..."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE —|TAX —

WHY IT WORKS Every other move in the Scorer system is an action. This one is restraint. Under pressure, the natural response is to fill silence with words. Every word spoken from a position of pressure costs Profit. The scorer who can sit in the silence while the other side talks has the highest sustainable Profit position in any negotiation. The Patience Play cannot be faked — it requires genuine comfort with not knowing the outcome.

The first person to fill the silence loses leverage.

MOVE 09 · THE PATH FORWARD

WHEN TO RUN IT A conversation has stalled.

Give the room a clear, specific, executable next step. Not a suggestion. A path. The person who creates movement controls the direction of movement.

THE SITUATION Negotiation stalled between buyer and seller:

"Here's what I suggest. We counter at list with their timeline and see how they respond."

PROFIT ▲▲|LOVE ▲▲|TAX ▼▼

WHY IT WORKS People follow the person who creates movement. When a conversation stalls, it is because both parties are protecting their position and neither is willing to move first. The Path Forward move creates a third option — not your position, not their position, but a next step that both parties can take without conceding. Profit builds because you are leading. Love builds because you are solving. Tax drops because the stalemate is broken.

Create the next step. People follow the person who creates movement.

The 9 Moves: Quick Reference

The move you need is determined by which score is failing.

pages.title: PART FOUR
pages.html:
PART FOUR

The Conversations

Scored in real time. Every pairing. Every move labeled.

BUYER / AGENT

The Showing

Where the decision is made before the offer is written

Marcus has been with his agent Dana for six weeks. Three previous showings, no offers. This is the fourth house. Price is at the top of his range.

◆

Dana: "I want to tell you something before we go in. The sellers are motivated — they've already bought their next place."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 74 ▲ 8|LOVE 62 ▲ 6|TAX 28 —

MOVE INTELLIGENCE TRANSFER

Dana ran Move 03 before the showing started. Marcus now has a negotiating anchor before he's seen a single room. Profit and Love both build simultaneously.

Marcus: "How motivated are we talking."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 76 ▲ 2|LOVE 62 —|TAX 28 —

MOVE PROBE — PROFIT ACCUMULATION

Marcus tested the ceiling of the information. He revealed nothing. Pure Profit move.

Dana: "Motivated enough that if the offer is clean and the timeline works, they might take less than list."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 76 —|LOVE 66 ▲ 4|TAX 30 ▲ 2

MOVE HONEST QUALIFICATION — LOVE BUILD

The word "might" is the Honest Strike in miniature. She did not oversell. Love builds because she did not exaggerate to close.

Marcus: "I like it. My wife hasn't seen it yet."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 73 ▼ 3|LOVE 66 —|TAX 38 ▲ 8

MOVE FAMILY SIGNAL — TAX ALERT

The deal just got conditional. Profit drops because Marcus revealed a dependency. Tax jumps. Dana's next move determines this transaction.

Dana: "Can we get her here this week? I want her to feel it too."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 78 ▲ 5|LOVE 74 ▲ 8|TAX 26 ▼ 12

MOVE FAMILY INCLUSION — MOVE 07

Dana ran Move 07 immediately. All three scores moved in the right direction simultaneously. This is the highest-value single move in this conversation.

AGENT / SELLER

The Listing Appointment

Where the relationship is won or lost before the contract is signed

Jordan is competing against two other agents for the Kellerman listing. They have lived in the house for eighteen years.

◆

Mr. Kellerman: "The last agent told us we could get 780."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 60 ▼ 10|LOVE 52 ▼ 2|TAX 38 ▲ 8

MOVE ANCHOR — PROFIT TRAP

The competing anchor was placed specifically to control the frame. Profit drops sharply. Jordan's next line is the most important of the appointment.

Jordan: "I'd be concerned about an agent who told you that before seeing the comps together."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 72 ▲ 12|LOVE 60 ▲ 8|TAX 28 ▼ 10

MOVE FRAME RESET — MOVE 01

Jordan ran Move 01. She did not attack the number — she attacked the process that produced it. Profit recovers significantly. The conversation has moved from price competition to process credibility.

Mr. Kellerman: "She seemed pretty confident."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 72 —|LOVE 60 —|TAX 34 ▲ 6

MOVE PUSHBACK — TAX BUILD

The Kellermans are defending the competitor. This is the critical branch. Jordan must decide: press or redirect. Pressing risks Love. Redirecting might surrender Profit.

Jordan: "I want you to get the most this house can actually deliver. Let me show you the last six months of sales on your block — you tell me what number you see."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 84 ▲ 12|LOVE 72 ▲ 12|TAX 18 ▼ 16

MOVE EVIDENCE MIRROR — MOVE 04

Move 04 at maximum expression. Jordan transferred the pricing conclusion to the Kellermans. They own the number now. She won the listing appointment in this one move.

BUYER / LOAN OFFICER

The Pre-Approval Call

Where the financial confidence of the entire transaction is set

First-time buyer Renee. Loan officer Chris. Three days before she wants to make an offer.

◆

Chris: "Your pre-approval is solid. The income documentation came back clean."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 68 —|LOVE 58 ▲ 4|TAX 24 —

MOVE CONFIRMATION — BASELINE LOVE

Good news delivered correctly. Love builds. But the move is expected — not powerful yet.

Renee: "Okay good. So we're all set?"

THE SCORE

PROFIT 68 —|LOVE 58 —|TAX 34 ▲ 10

MOVE CERTAINTY SEEK — TAX SPIKE

"Are we all set" is the moment Chris must choose: false certainty or honest qualification. This is the branch that determines whether Chris is a professional or a salesperson.

Chris: "Mostly. There are two conditions on the file I want you to know about before you make the offer. Nothing that should stop the deal — but you need to understand them."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 68 —|LOVE 76 ▲ 18|TAX 22 ▼ 12

MOVE HONEST STRIKE — MOVE 02

Move 02 in its purest form. "Mostly" instead of "yes." Conditions named before they become surprises. Love jumps 18 points — the highest single-move Love gain in this book. This is the move that makes Renee refer Chris to every buyer she knows for the next five years.

AGENT / LOAN OFFICER

The Pipeline Call

Where deals are built before they exist

Agent Devon. Loan officer Maria. Marcus is sixty days from being ready to buy.

◆

Devon: "I want to get ahead of this one. Marcus is close but not ready. What does he need to do in the next 60 days to make this file clean?"

THE SCORE

PROFIT 76 ▲ 8|LOVE 70 ▲ 4|TAX 16 ▼ 6

MOVE PROACTIVE PLANNING — PROFIT DOMINANT

Devon ran Move 03 on the professional relationship. He gave Maria something before she had to ask for it: preparation time. This is BDM-level thinking applied to the Agent/LO partnership.

Maria: "Two things. His debt-to-income is borderline — if he can pay one card down it moves him to a cleaner tier. And 60 days of bank statements with no large undocumented deposits."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 80 ▲ 4|LOVE 78 ▲ 8|TAX 12 ▼ 4

MOVE SPECIFIC INTELLIGENCE — HIGHEST LO MOVE

Maria gave Devon specific, actionable intelligence. Love between Agent and LO reaches its highest point. The file will arrive clean. The deal will close. This partnership will compound across years of transactions.

SELLER / NEGOTIATION

The Counter

Where emotional anchors get converted to executable positions

The Patels received an offer $34,000 under asking. Their agent Sandra is walking them through the response.

◆

Mrs. Patel: "That offer is insulting."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 58 —|LOVE 58 —|TAX 42 ▲ 10

MOVE EMOTIONAL ANCHOR — TAX CRITICAL

The word "insulting" is a Tax signal. The negotiation is now running on dignity rather than data. This is the hardest type of negotiation to close.

Sandra: "I understand that feeling. But I want to tell you what the offer actually says — not what the number looks like, but what the buyer's position actually is."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 64 ▲ 6|LOVE 68 ▲ 10|TAX 30 ▼ 12

MOVE FRAME RESET + HONEST STRIKE — MOVES 01 & 02

Sandra ran two moves simultaneously. Frame Reset to change the category from "insulting" to "buyer's position." Honest Strike implicit in "not what the number looks like." This is the double-move — the most powerful tool in the Scorer system.

Sandra: "They are pre-approved, no contingencies except inspection, can close in 21 days. That's a clean offer. The number is low but the structure is what you wanted. Counter at list with their timeline."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 80 ▲ 16|LOVE 72 ▲ 4|TAX 18 ▼ 12

MOVE PATH FORWARD — MOVE 09

Move 09 at maximum expression. Sandra did not ask the Patels what they wanted to do. She gave them the path. Profit reaches its peak in this conversation because Sandra is now leading both sides of the negotiation simultaneously.

BUYER / FAMILY

The Kitchen Table

The conversation the agent never sees but always loses to

9pm. Elena and David have been to a showing. Elena is telling her mother Rosa about the house.

◆

Rosa: "How much are they asking?"

THE SCORE

PROFIT 58 ▼ 6|LOVE 62 —|TAX 44 ▲ 10

MOVE PRICE ANCHOR — TAX INTRODUCTION

Rosa's first question is the price. Without the context of the showing experience, the number will be compared to something irrelevant. This is how family members kill deals they never attended.

Elena: "Five-eighty. But Dana says the sellers are motivated and there might be room."

THE SCORE

PROFIT 62 ▲ 4|LOVE 62 —|TAX 40 ▼ 4

MOVE AGENT PROXY — INTELLIGENCE TRANSFER BY PROXY

pages.title: PART FOUR (cont. 2)
pages.html:
Elena is carrying Dana's Move 03 into the family conversation. This is why building Love with the buyer matters. The agent who the buyer trusts becomes the agent who wins the family conversation without being in the room.

Rosa: "Five-eighty is too much. When we bought in '98—"

THE SCORE

PROFIT 50 ▼ 12|LOVE 62 —|TAX 58 ▲ 18

MOVE HISTORICAL ANCHOR — CRITICAL COLLAPSE

1998 prices applied to 2024 reality. Tax spikes to critical. Elena will carry this doubt into tomorrow's conversation with Dana. The scorer's diagnosis: Dana needs to run a market education session that includes Rosa before the next showing.

David: "What did the neighborhood feel like?"

THE SCORE

PROFIT 54 ▲ 4|LOVE 66 ▲ 4|TAX 48 ▼ 10

MOVE REDIRECT — PRESSURE REVEAL BY PROXY

David shifted the frame from price to experience. This is Move 06 run instinctively by a non-professional. The scorer notes David as a positive influence and advises Dana to include him directly.

pages.title: PART FIVE
pages.html:
PART FIVE

The Drills

Score before you read the answer. Train the eye, not the memory.

Read the line. Identify which scores move and in which direction. Then read the answer. The goal is not to match the number exactly — the goal is to train yourself to see which score is moving before the answer tells you.

DRILL 01

"We're just looking today."

Who gains Profit from this line? What is the Intent?

ANSWER P Buyer +6 · L −2 · T −4

Buyer Profit +6. Frame move. The buyer is establishing low-commitment positioning to prevent the agent from reading genuine interest. Intent is to reduce the agent's leverage. Love drops because the buyer does not yet fully trust the agent. This line always opens the same way: agent must run Move 03 to rebuild Profit parity.

DRILL 02

"I've been doing this for twenty-two years."

What score is moving? For whom? And what is the hidden risk?

ANSWER P Agent +8 · L 0 · T +6

Agent Profit +8. Tax +6. Credential move. Profit builds — experience is leverage. But Tax builds simultaneously because the agent has created an expectation they must consistently deliver. An agent who says this and then makes a basic error pays double the Love penalty they would otherwise.

DRILL 03

"The sellers are flexible on the closing date."

Score the move. Which move number is the agent running?

ANSWER P Buyer +10 · L 0 · T −8

Buyer Profit +10, Tax −8. Move 03 — Intelligence Transfer. One of the highest Profit-per-line moves in the transaction. The flexibility reduces timeline risk immediately and gives the buyer a structural advantage in the offer conversation.

DRILL 04

"My husband really loves it but I'm not sure about the commute."

What is the scorer's immediate priority after this line?

ANSWER P −6 · L 0 · T +8

Buyer Profit −6, Tax +8. Split decision signal. The decision has just become conditional on an objection that was not previously in the conversation. The scorer's priority: run Move 06 — Pressure Reveal. "Is the commute the main concern, or is there something else?" Surface the real objection before it becomes the reason the deal dies.

DRILL 05

"I should have caught that issue earlier. That's on me."

What move is this? What score moves most dramatically?

ANSWER P +4 · L +18 · T +4

Move 05 — Ownership Move. Love +18. The most powerful single move in the Scorer system. Owning an error without explanation disarms the other party, builds more Love than almost any other single line, and holds the Profit position because the person who takes responsibility first holds the frame. Tax increases because responsibility was accepted — but the Love gain dominates completely.

DRILL 06

"Let me see what I can do."

Is this a Profit move, Love move, or Tax move? Whose score changes most?

ANSWER P Agent −4 · L −2 · T +8

Agent Tax +8. The most dangerous phrase in professional conversations. Not a commitment. Not a refusal. An implicit promise the agent may not be able to keep. Tax builds because the expectation was created. Love drops because the client registers the non-commitment. Profit drops because the agent moved from expert to errand runner. Replace it with Move 09: give a specific path instead of a vague offer.

DRILL 07

"The only other offer came in at 560."

What just happened to the Buyer's Profit and Tax?

ANSWER P Buyer +14 · L 0 · T −12

Buyer Profit +14, Tax −12. Competing offer anchor by the agent. When a buyer hears there is another offer, their decision ambiguity collapses. Profit builds because the market has given them their floor. Tax drops because the "what should I offer" uncertainty has been replaced by "what do I need to do to win."

DRILL 08

"I'm not going to pressure you — take whatever time you need."

What is happening to the agent's Profit? Why is this dangerous?

ANSWER P Agent −8 · L +4 · T 0

Agent Profit −8, Love +4. Feels like a client-first move. Emotionally it is. But strategically it is Profit surrender. The agent has removed urgency from a transaction where urgency creates decisions. Love builds — clients appreciate the absence of pressure. But the agent just gave away their most powerful tool for moving a buyer off "we need to think about it." Run Move 09 instead: create a path that makes the decision easy, not optional.

pages.title: PART SIX
pages.html:
PART SIX

The Field Guide

What to watch. What it means. What to do. Carry this into the room.

At The Showing

THE BUYER SLOWS DOWN IN ONE ROOM

WATCH Client pace drops in a specific room compared to others.

MEANS The room they slow down in is the room they are deciding about. Everything else is evaluation. This room is negotiation.

YOUR MOVE Stop narrating. Let the silence run. Do not fill it. The buyer filling the silence is the most valuable information in the showing.

WE NEED TO THINK ABOUT IT

WATCH Client disengages at end of showing.

MEANS Either Love is not high enough for them to trust the decision, or there is unnamed Tax — a concern they have not said out loud.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 06: "Is there something you need to know that you don't know yet?" Not "what are your concerns." What do you need to know. That question surfaces the real objection.

MY PARTNER HASN'T SEEN IT

WATCH Decision dependency revealed mid-showing.

MEANS The deal cannot close without the partner. Everything from here is staging for a conversation you are not in.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 07 immediately. Do not suggest — make it easy. "Can we get them here Thursday evening? I'll make sure it works."

At The Offer

BUYER ASKS WHAT YOU THINK THEY SHOULD OFFER

WATCH Decision transferred to the agent.

MEANS Love account is at its highest point. The buyer trusts you more than their own analysis. This is the highest-influence moment in the transaction.

YOUR MOVE Give a specific number with a specific reason. Not a range. Run Move 09. Conviction is the offer.

SELLER COUNTER IS NEAR LIST DESPITE LOW OFFER

WATCH Counter did not engage with the offer position.

MEANS The seller is anchored to a number with emotional weight. The counter is not a negotiating position — it is a statement of value.

YOUR MOVE Do not counter the counter immediately. Run Move 06: ask the listing agent what timeline flexibility looks like. Move the conversation from price to structure.

LISTING AGENT GOES SILENT AFTER THE OFFER

WATCH Communication has stopped after submission.

MEANS Either another offer came in, the seller is deliberating, or the listing agent is managing a difficult principal.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 08 — the Patience Play. Then call, do not text. Ask: "Is there anything my clients can provide that would help the decision?" Client-first framing that simultaneously gets you information.

At The Negotiation

EMOTIONAL LANGUAGE ABOUT THE OFFER

WATCH Words like "insulting," "low-ball," "unreasonable" enter the conversation.

MEANS Negotiating from emotion rather than data. Emotional negotiators reveal more than strategic ones.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 01 — Frame Reset. "Let me show you what the market supports and then we can look at the offer in that context." Data vs. emotion — data wins if you hold the frame.

THE NEGOTIATION STALLS

WATCH Multiple rounds of counter with no movement.

MEANS Both parties are protecting Profit at the cost of closing. Continued negotiation is costing both parties more than the gap between them.

YOUR MOVE Name the gap in dollars per day. Make the Tax of not closing visible. Then run Move 09 — give the room a path.

THE OTHER SIDE SAYS "LET ME THINK ABOUT IT"

WATCH Conversation has been paused indefinitely.

MEANS Either the price is wrong, the Trust is insufficient, or there is unnamed Tax. "Think about it" almost never means what it says.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 06 before they leave: "Before you go — is there something that would make this easier to decide?" One question. The real objection almost always surfaces.

At The Closing

COLD FEET BEFORE CLOSING

WATCH Buyer energy drops in final 72 hours. Questions increase.

MEANS This is normal Tax response. The largest transaction of their life is about to become real. The questions are not about the house — they are about the decision.

YOUR MOVE Do not reassure with enthusiasm. Validate with facts. Run Move 02: "The feeling you have right now is appropriate. Here is what we have confirmed is true." Facts over feelings.

LOAN CONDITION SURFACES IN FINAL WEEK

WATCH Underwriting condition appears close to closing.

MEANS Buyer's Tax is about to spike. Trust in the process is being tested. How this is handled in the next hour determines whether the deal closes.

YOUR MOVE Call the buyer before the loan officer does if at all possible. Run Move 02 — Honest Strike first. "There is a condition on the file. Here is exactly what it is, here is exactly what it requires, here is the timeline." Own the information.

The transaction is not a transaction.

It is a ledger.

Every line you said, every move you ran, every score you moved in the right direction — it accumulates. The scorer does not just close deals. The scorer builds a career that does not require starting over every quarter because the Love accounts are full, the Profit position is established, and the Tax has been managed so well that clients do not come back with problems — they come back with people.

Nine moves. That is the complete executable layer of the PLT doctrine.

Frame Reset. Honest Strike. Intelligence Transfer. Evidence Mirror. Ownership Move. Pressure Reveal. Family Inclusion. Patience Play. Path Forward.

Under pressure the brain can remember nine things if they are named correctly. They are named correctly. They are yours.

Profit. Love. Tax.

Every conversation. Real time.

About the Author

Craig Jones is the founder of the PLT Framework and the architect of the PLT Doctrine Series. He writes under the name Little Bunny. He built the framework from years of direct observation — watching how transactions actually work, what actually gets exchanged when two people negotiate, what actually collapses a deal that should have closed, what actually saves one that should have died. The PLT Framework is the systematic account of what he observed.

The 9 Dominant PLT Moves is the executable layer of the full doctrine.
